notes: The ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025 and was on the December 2, 2025 council agenda (per the file name); the document states no effective date and no adoption date for the second reading, so effective_date is left blank. Penalties are up to $1,000 per violation, enforceable by the City Attorney or aggrieved tenants.

Two records extracted: the state screening-fee cap and rules (Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6, as summarized by the City page) and the Berkeley local ordinance (BMC ch. 13.78). The page describes state law (AB 12, Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5) and the Berkeley Rent Ordinance interest requirement. Two records are output: the CA state deposit rule and the Berkeley interest rule. The Berkeley interest rule is cited by the name the page uses because no specific code section is given. The page gives no effective date for the Berkeley interest requirement. The page does not name Civ. Code § 1950.5 explicitly; it names only Assembly Bill 12, so the citation is the bill.

Notice describes the 2026 AGA order (Rent Board Regulation 1148) under Berkeley's rent stabilization program. Building-level coverage and exemptions are not stated in the notice, so coverage is left empty. The notice says the increase may be taken no earlier than January 1, 2026.

The document is a coverage guide table, not the ordinance text, and says it is only a guide. No ordinance section numbers, cap amounts, or effective dates are given, so effective_date is blank and confidence is moderate. Two records were extracted (rent control and just cause) with shared coverage. Security deposit interest coverage is mentioned but no deposit rule (amount, rate, deadline) is stated, so no security_deposits record was created. The table lists both a 'built before 1980' multifamily rule and a 'Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980' rule, which leaves a gap for units built in 1980 itself; the document does not resolve this, so the coverage cutoff of 1980-01-01 is a best reading of 'before 1980'.

The policy applies only to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; it is a city agency policy, not a citywide ordinance. No effective date is stated beyond the February 2017 document date, so effective_date is left blank. The credit-score restriction is folded into this single screening_restrictions instrument. Federal or state criminal history requirements preempt the policy.

The bill text is not included on this page; the record is based on the bill title and status only. The bill is from the 193rd (2023-2024) session, which has ended, and its history shows it was accompanied by a study order (H5035) on 9/9/2024 with no enactment, so it is recorded as failed. The title covers both rent stabilization and eviction protections, but only one record is output because the page gives no instrument-level detail; a separate just_cause_eviction record is not made since the page does not describe specific eviction rules.

The page is a general fair housing overview and cites no ordinance or statute. The only in-scope rule is the protection against source-of-income (rental assistance) discrimination, recorded under screening_restrictions. No effective date, coverage conditions or exemptions are stated. The page's list of protected classes and complaint process are outside the six categories and were not extracted.

The Act is a notice-and-reporting requirement for tenancy terminations; it does not restrict eviction causes or halt eviction. It is nonetheless the closest in-scope item (just_cause_eviction: notice requirements for ending a tenancy), so one record is output with moderate confidence. The page gives no effective date and no coverage exemptions. Rent increase, deposit, fee, screening and algorithm rules are not present.

Single instrument extracted: Boston's Housing Stability Notification Act, a notice-procedure ordinance for terminating tenancies. It does not limit eviction causes, so it is categorized under just_cause_eviction as the closest in-scope category (eviction notice requirements). Effective date taken from the FAQ's statement; the ordinance citation is given as Sec. 10-11.7, which the document shows for enforcement. Lowered confidence because it is a notice requirement rather than a true just-cause regime.

The page is mostly general fair housing guidance (discrimination, accommodations, modifications, harassment), which is out of scope. Two in-scope screening_restrictions rules were extracted under FEHA: source-of-income protection and criminal-history screening limits. The page gives no effective dates and names FEHA without a specific section number, so citation is the Act's name. No rent, eviction, deposit, fee, or algorithmic pricing rules appear.

The bill is a general antitrust measure and does not mention rental housing, landlords or rents. It is recorded as an algorithmic_rent_setting rule because its definition of 'common pricing algorithm' (software using competitor data to recommend or set prices) is broad enough to reach rent-setting software, but the text itself does not say so. Approved by the Governor on October 6, 2025 with no urgency clause stated, so the California default effective date of January 1, 2026 is applied. Section 16756.1 (pleading standard) is procedural and out of scope.

Only the just-cause eviction rule is in this section; the rent cap in Civ. Code § 1947.12 is referenced but not stated, so no rent_increase_limits record was extracted. Section is operative April 1, 2024, and the amending act (AB 1529) took effect January 1, 2026; the section sunsets January 1, 2030. The date used is the stated operative date. Exemption for owner-occupied and alienable-separate properties depends on owner type and written notice, which cannot be tested with building facts. The 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption is modeled as a rolling test.

Only the rent cap in § 1947.12 is in scope; the section also cross-references just-cause (§ 1946.2) and § 1947.13, but their text is not included here. Section was added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 290 (SB 567), effective January 1, 2024 and operative April 1, 2024 by its own provisions; it is repealed as of January 1, 2030. Subdivision (h) applies the cap to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (Feb. 18, 2021 for mobilehome tenancies), reflecting the predecessor version of the law. Coverage exemptions for owner type, affordable housing, dormitories, and local rent control are mapped to 'other' or 'owner_type' facts, which cannot be tested with available building data.

One record for the single instrument (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5). Return deadline (21 calendar days), photograph requirements, the $125 itemization threshold, the ban on 'nonrefundable' deposit language and bad-faith damages (up to twice the deposit) are folded into the one record. The text shows the 2024-07-01 date from subdivision (c)(6) and the 2026-01-01 date of the latest amendment; the section's cap provisions are recorded with the July 1, 2024 date because (c)(6) says the subdivision does not apply to security collected before July 1, 2024. The document does not state the effective date of the cap itself in a standalone sentence, so reviewers may wish to confirm it against the chaptered bill (AB 12).

One instrument (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6) in one category. Fee cap (adjusted annually for CPI), no-fee-without-available-unit rule, first-qualified-applicant or full-refund processes, itemized receipt, and credit report copy are details of the same rule and are captured in the requirement text. The statute applies to residential rental property generally and states no coverage exemptions in this section.

Only the source-of-income provisions (subdivisions (a), (n), (o), (p)) fall within the screening_restrictions category; the remaining protected-class discrimination provisions are outside the six in-scope categories. Section text states it was amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776 (SB 267), effective January 1, 2024; the original effective date of the source-of-income protection is not stated in this document.

Part 1 of 2; the text ends mid-section (155-23), so later provisions, including vacancy decontrol, registration and condo/co-op owner-occupant provisions, are not in this part. This section governs termination of a lease for nonpayment of rent. The section governs notice to terminate tenancies at will (three months' notice generally; 14-day notice for nonpayment with a one-time cure right). The only arguably related content is the nonpayment notice and cure mechanics, which is a termination-notice rule, not a just-cause regime, so no records were extracted.
